source_text: Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Iesu, in mortem ipsius baptizati sumus. Consepulti enim sumus cum illo per baptismum in mortem, ut quomodo surrexit Christus a mortuis, ita et nos in novitate vitae ambulemus.
thought_title: Baptism as burial with Christ into death and walking in newness of life
orientation: Origen is quoting Paul's words from Romans 6 about what baptism means for believers.
pass_a_gloss: Whoever [we] have been baptized in Christ Jesus, into [the] death of him [we] have been baptized. [We] have been buried together for with him through baptism into death, so that just as rose Christ from [the] dead, so also we in newness of life may walk.

choices.english: we may walk in newness of life
choices.why: Keeps the literal noun 'newness' and the verb 'walk' as a metaphor for conduct, matching the source's concrete imagery.
rejected: we might live a new life
we should lead a new life

choices.why: Renders the compound verb literally, preserving the 'together with' prefix that links believers to Christ's burial.
Literal rendering of the plural 'the dead', standard for resurrection language.
Captures the inclusive force of 'whoever' applied to the first-person plural 'we have been baptized'.

bible_refs.note: Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Iesu, in mortem ipsius baptizati sumus. Consepulti enim sumus cum illo per baptismum in mortem, ut quomodo surrexit Christus a mortuis, ita et nos in novitate vitae ambulemus.

pass_b_english: All of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death. For we were buried together with him through baptism into death, so that just as Christ rose from the dead, we too may walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3-4).
